verdict: Globe Life grew total premium revenue 7% to $1.31B and earned $361M; EPS of $4.62 was a shade below last year's $4.73 because this year's reserve-review gains were smaller.

segments.name: Life premium
segments.note: Life-insurance premiums — American Income is the largest source ($471M of life premium by channel detail in the release's margin tables).

segments.name: Health premium
segments.note: Health-insurance premiums (supplemental health and Medicare supplement) — up 16%, the growth engine this quarter.

segments.name: Investment & other income, net
segments.note: Net investment income of $295.9M (interest and dividends on the portfolio backing future claims), plus $1.2M of other income, less $12.6M of realized investment losses.

opex.name: Commissions & acquisition costs
opex.note: Commissions, premium taxes and acquisition costs that are not deferred.

opex.name: Amortization of deferred acquisition costs
opex.note: Spreading the cost of winning policies (mainly agent commissions) over the policies' lives.

opex.name: Other operating expense
opex.note: Running the company day to day.

footerNote: Insurer layout (the same one our Chubb pages use): revenue is premiums plus investment income, and the direct cost is policyholder benefits — claims and reserve increases. 'Operating profit' here is Globe Life's pre-tax income of $441M; the company has no separate operating-income line. Total premium was $1,311M (+7%); segment premium detail is from the release's GAAP statement of operations.

takeaways.title: Health premiums are the growth engine
takeaways.text: Health premium rose 16% to $447M — Family Heritage health underwriting margin rose 12% and United American had an underwriting loss on Medicare Supplement claims timing — while life premium grew a steadier 2%.

takeaways.title: Operating EPS vs $4.62 GAAP
takeaways.text: Net operating income — Globe Life's preferred measure, which excludes realized investment results — was $379M, or $4.84 a share. GAAP EPS of $4.62 includes a $10.0M after-tax realized loss and $6.8M of legal-proceedings costs.

takeaways.title: Reserve reviews flatter benefits
takeaways.text: Policyholder benefits include about $146M of pre-tax favorable remeasurement gains from the annual assumption update ($117M life, $29M health) — slightly less than last year's $158M, which is the main reason profit dipped.

oneTimers: Benefits are net of total remeasurement gains of $145.8M before tax from the annual reserve-assumption update ($116.7M life, $29.1M health), versus $158.3M a year ago.
Realized investment losses were $12.6M before tax; legal-proceedings costs were $6.8M after tax (both excluded from net operating income).
Globe Life repurchased 1.1M shares in the quarter for $185M.
